🌧️ Flooding in California and Florida, along with storms in the northeastern United States, are complicating travel starting Monday ahead of Thanksgiving on November 26, when more than 80 million travelers are expected to hit the road. 🌊 In California, the Coastal Commission warned of “exceptionally high tides” (king tides) between November 24 and 26, which—combined with storms bringing up to 7.6 centimeters of rain and winds of 72 kilometers per hour—prompted San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie to urge residents to avoid nonessential travel. 🚨 In Florida, Governor Ron DeSantis announced that he will request federal aid following rains of up to 51 centimeters and hundreds of rescues, while the National Weather Service (NWS) has issued alerts for North Carolina and the Northeast.

🚢 Fishermen from Ecuador whose boats were intercepted and sunk on the high seas by U.S. forces will file lawsuits against the Ecuadorian government for alleged failure to defend them, attorney Juan Alberto Alvia announced in statements on Monday, November 23. 🔍 According to the Permanent Committee for the Defense of Human Rights (CDH), 206 seafarers were subjected to arbitrary detention, torture, and the destruction of their vessels by the U.S. between the Galápagos Islands and the mainland coast, while eight crew members of the vessel Fiorella have remained missing since January. 🏛️ Alvia denounced the lack of assistance from Daniel Noboa’s administration and noted that U.S. lawyers are considering representing the victims, following the acquittal—due to lack of evidence—of some 40 fishermen accused of criminal conspiracy.
